I'm 38 years old, been farming 13 mu here in Quzhou for 15 years. I finished middle school, so I can read the fertilizer bags and understand what the extension agent says, but I'm not doing any fancy calculations. My household is three people — me, my wife, and my father. My wife works at the cardboard box factory in town during the week, which brings in steady cash but means me and my old man handle most of the field work. She helps with cotton picking on weekends though.

I've got about 8 mu in wheat-maize double cropping and about 5 mu in cotton. Money's always tight. My wife's wages cover household costs, but the farm has to pay for itself. I probably can't spend more than about 6,000 yuan on inputs this year or I'll have no cash cushion if something goes wrong.

**Wheat:** I planted last October, same as always. Used Jinmai 22, an improved variety — cost about 40 yuan per mu for seed. Before planting I put down base fertilizer, about 45 kg of compound fertilizer per mu. Then at green-up in March I topdressed with urea. The extension fellow says 15 kg of nitrogen per mu is enough, and that's roughly what I applied — one bag of compound plus some urea gets me there. I don't use scales; I know what a mu looks like. The wheat looks decent this year, not amazing but not bad. I'll irrigate three times total — the winter irrigation, one at jointing, and one more around heading if it stays dry. Pumping costs about 20 yuan per mu each time, so I don't water for nothing. Me and my father handle all the wheat work. Hoping for about 400 kg per mu, same as last year if the weather holds.

**Cotton:** I'm keeping 5 mu of cotton because Lao Wang down the road did well with it last year and the price was alright. I'm planting hybrid seed next week — costs about 50 yuan per mu. I'll put compound fertilizer in the planting furrow, about 35 kg per mu, then topdress with urea twice: once at flowering and once at boll-setting. That comes to about 14 kg of nitrogen per mu total. I'll irrigate twice — at flowering and boll-setting. Cotton is thirsty but pumping fuel is expensive, so two times is my limit unless it's a drought year. The big cost with cotton is labor. My wife helps pick on weekends, but for the main picking in September and October I'll need to hire two women from the village for about 6 days. That's 100 yuan per day each. I'm expecting about 250 kg of seed cotton per mu.

**Maize:** After wheat harvest in mid-June, I've got maybe 5 days before the season gets too late. I'll rotary-till the wheat stubble quick and plant Zhengdan 958 hybrid seed — it's what everyone uses, costs about 45 yuan per mu. At planting I'll put down about 40 kg of compound fertilizer per mu, then topdress with urea when the plants are knee-high. Total nitrogen is about 16 kg per mu. The extension people say you can get by with less, but I'd rather waste a bit of fertilizer than risk a bad harvest — a bad year hurts more than a good year helps. Maize doesn't need much water; I'll irrigate twice, once at the big trumpet stage and once at filling if it's dry. For harvest, me and my father usually handle it, but if we're pressed for time I might hire a combine operator for a day or two.

The tradeoff I'm always managing is cash versus safety. I'd like to put more fertilizer on everything, but I need to keep enough yuan in my pocket for fuel, hired picking labor, and emergencies. So I stick to what worked last year, add a small safety margin, and hope the weather cooperates.

For wheat I follow last year's plan — improved seed, compound base plus urea topdress, about 15 kg nitrogen per mu, three irrigations. Cotton is my cash crop bet this year; hybrid seed, two topdressings, two irrigations, but hired picking labor is expensive so I have to watch those costs. Maize after wheat is all about speed — rotary till, plant Zhengdan 958, compound at planting plus one urea topdress, two irrigations.
